column1: # hypothesis: THE ONE MEASURED MITIGATION IN THIS AREA IS CHEAP AND THE PROBLEM IT MITIGATES HAS NEVER BEEN MEASURED UNDER DESTRUCTION. k-DOP clipping (10.1145/3681758.3697996) replaces TAA's axis-aligned neighbourhood clamp with a tighter k-discrete-oriented polytope at 0.2 ms overhead (GPU NOT NAMED IN THE ABSTRACT)
column2: and its framing is that prior bounding-box methods are 'only situationally effective'. Separately
column3: Epic's account of virtual shadow maps in Fortnite says animated deformation invalidates shadow pages and that they ABANDONED CACHING FOR DIRECTIONAL SUN SHADOWS ENTIRELY -- with no invalidation cost published anywhere. This experiment measures the destruction half; P-79 measures the shadow half. (C1) In game_dig
column4: the fraction of TAA history samples rejected in the frame after a brush stroke is at least 5x the steady-state rejection rate
column5: and the elevated rate persists for at least 3 frames. (C2) k-DOP clipping recovers at least half the rejected samples at under 0.3 ms. (C3) The rejection is SPATIALLY CONCENTRATED at the brush
column6: not global: over 80% of rejected samples fall within the brush's screen-space bounding box dilated by one dig radius. SHARE: C1 is a rate
column7: not a ratio of a total; C2 moves the TAA resolve stage.
